name: Classic Nob Hill Studio - Roof Deck
description:
A cute studio with nice street views and lots of light and easy access to a shared roof deck with awesome Golden Gate views.

Great, classic "Old Frisco" neighborhood.

New double-pane windows help keep out the sounds of the city.
neighborhood_overview:
Very centrally located.

Fishermans Wharf, Chinatown, North Beach, downtown, Union Square shopping, Polk Street action, are all within walking distant.

For those who prefer to ride, public transport, including the classic cable car lines, are conveniently close.

Nob Hill is Old San Francisco, filled with the cable cars and classic Victorian architecture the city is famous for.

It's also a rich neighborhood with luxury buildings and nice restaurants and expansive views of the bay and beyond. There are a Trader Joes and a Whole Foods within walking distance, not to mention a cute gourmet market on the corner one block up.

For the party-minded, Polk Street and its remarkable night life are just three blocks away.
host_about:
I'm a writer, and encourage visiting writers and editors to use this studio. This is a historic building on Nob Hill, convenient to everything. Dashiell Hammett lived in this building and, we are told, finished The Maltese Falcon here. We bought this studio to house our son while he was in college; now we rent it to tourists and visiting professionals.

We are very interested in swapping housing also.

There are many options for dining and just about every type of world cuisine is found in the excellent neighborhood restaurants--this is not an exaggeration. Please take a moment to look at our recommendations in our Host Guidebook which features our favorite places.

In addition to dining options, the area is brimming with cafes, sports bars, retail shops, a post office, hardware store, drug store, laundromats, bakeries, a grocery market, and banks all within a five minute walk from the suite. host_about:

~Syl and Art

My favorite restaurant is Zazie at 941 Cole Street with excellent brunch on weekends and lunch on weekdays. Both places are only a five-minute walk.

There are three pizza restaurants on Haight Street. The best one is Bizza on Haight Street near Masonic Street.

Check the book "Stairway Walks in San Francisco". There are many artful stairway walks throughout the city that originate near our house. Cafe's and restaurants are a 20-30 minute walk away in any direction.

host_about:
I am a physician and I moved to USA 22 years ago. I love what San Francisco city and the Bay Area has to offer. I feel very lucky and privileged to live in a beautiful and safe area of San Francisco called Pacific Heights. 

I am an avid mountaineer/climber and I travel usually once a year, for a month - long expedition trip. That is usually when I open the calendar in AirBnB for my apartment, as well as (separately) for my garage. 

I would like to rent my beautiful home to someone reliable for all that time when I am gone. 

The things I can't live without are my family, friends, mountains, my amazing home, nature, meditation and any kind of physical activity daily. 

My favorite travel destinations - to many to mention. I feel amazing in high altitude mountains. 

I climbed all the highest mountains in the world called Seven Summits (including Mt.Everest), as well as skied to the South Pole.  Beside that, all my travels and expeditions left me with amazing memories. 

My favorite books - too many to list here as I  read a lot, but I love the most  "Master and Margarita" by Michail Bulhakov. There are many books in my home, so if you have time feel free to read something new. I switched now to ebooks or audiobooks, as it doesn't take any physical space. 

My favorite food is prepared with local and organic ingredients - check out many restaurants on Fillmore street - you will have so many to choose from, even after Pandemic years. I love sushi and the best sushi in the city is a walking distance from my home - check out Tataki restaurant (on California street/Divisadero street) - amazing and fresh! 
I also would encourage you to check “State Bird Provisions”, but you would need a reservation. It’s a 7 -10 minutes walking distance from my home. Located on Fillmore street. 

I travel a lot for business - Marriott hotels, but for fun - I prefer staying in a tent or in a cool Airbnb place in different cities all over the world.

About the Inner Mission District-
"La Mision" / The MIssion
Centrally located close to downtown, it is the city's Latino district & has been the gateway for most new immigrants, initially Italian, Irish, then predominantly Latino since the 1970's .
It is famous for its historic buildings, Mission burritos (the best in Northern California), grungy artistic scene & it's colorful murals.
Though the Mission still retains it's gritty 'barrio' (hood) flavor the neighborhood has been undergoing a second wave of gentrification, experiencing with an influx of techn money.
The Mission district is large & complex, with varying socioeconomic areas, clusters of mini-communities, and specialty stores found nowhere else. A few years back Utne Reader rated the Inner Mission the 2nd coolest place to live in the US (first was New Orlean's Garden District).
Like in any other cities there are sections of the Mission that can be high crime but don't let that scare you, a
host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.

host_about:
I live  alone in my our art filled home in the Lower Haight — central to everything. I retired from working downtown in Union Square; it takes very little effort to get there, three stops on MUNI. Our public-transit system is everywhere and very close to the house (be it a MUNI, the N Judah — underground — or the street car on Market Street). Our closest surrounding neighborhoods are Hayes Valley, Duboce Triangle, The Castro (just underwent extensive renovations), the Upper Haight and Valencia Street in the Mission District. On Waller Street we're literally steps away from some of the best food, bars and shopping (not tourist spots). The Lower Haight was voted the number one neighborhood in San Francisco by the tech community. Most important, do not rent a large car or let the car agency upgrade you to a larger car. Parking is too difficult. The rental agency tries to unload larger cars by offering visitors an upgrade. Don't accept it. I allow my guests to park in the street in front of my garage providing there is enough room.

My home (pre earthquake Edwardian) has been with me for more than forty years, so you can ask me anything that you want to know about the Bay Area and I am  bound to point you in the right direction. What else... Ah, just feel free to be in touch. I look forward to having you around! I just concluded my ninth year as a host on Airbnb. I am continually told that my price is too low. I am OK with my fee. I really want my guests to have a great time when staying in my home. To paraphrase the clothing designer Tom Ford, " Surrounding yourself with beautiful objects, enhances the quality of your life". It is my  unofficial motto. 

After hosting many guests from many different places, I learned that it is important to understand that when you book my home you are also experiencing my life. I have friends that stop by. I occasionally have people for dinner. It is essential to understand that I am not a professional innkeeper. I am not running a bed and breakfast. I am an Airbnb host who accept guests to stay in my guest bedrooms. I want my guests to live like residents of San Francisco. My neighborhood is very popular. When you stay with me you are returning to your San Francisco home.

host_about:
AnneKarin was born in Chicago to Henry P. and Elly Glass.  Theirs was an artistic household.  Henry was educated in the Wiener Werkstadt and was one of the founders of the field of Industrial Design in the U.S.  Elly was a member of the Viennese Dressmakers’ Guild.  Both of them taught at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.  AnneKarin grew up in Northfield IL and graduated from New Trier HS in 1961.  She received her BA in Anthropology from the University of Illinois, Urbana, in 1966 and joined the Peace Corps that same year.  She served as a Volunteer for three years in Ilheus, Bahia, Brazil, where she founded a leather working factory that provided steady work for local shoe makers.  Upon her return she went to Illinois Institute of Technology where she received an MA in Linguistics.
She tolerated the weather in Chicago until 1973 when she moved to San Francisco where Peace Corps friends facilitated her settlement into a new life on the West Coast.  Two months after she arrived she broke her leg in a ski accident and spent 11 months in a cast.  When able to walk again, she pursued a sign painting business which grew into a brokerage for architectural graphics.  From that she moved into print brokering, specializing in 3-D displays.  This enabled her to buy the house she was living in on Potrero Hill in San Francisco.
The recession in 1989 plus the introduction of computer technology into the world of print created a crossroad.  AnneKarin decided to give up the printing business and return to graduate school where she earned a graduate certificate in Educational Therapy.  She specialized in perception/cognition and opened a private practice, helping children and adults with learning disabilities to address the underlying causes of their learning problems.  
During all these years AnneKarin continued to pursue visual art.  Today she works as an artist, focusing on the figure.  When no model is available she enjoys painting still lifes, abstracts, and landscapes.  She has shown her work internationally and in many competitions across the U.S.  She is a member of the Artists’ Guild of San Francisco.
AnneKarin lives with Clebia, whom she met in Ilheus when she was a Peace Corps volunteer. Clebia is a case worker for intellectually challenged adults and a gourmet cook.  Clebia and AnneKarin enjoy travel, walking in the outdoors, fine dining, music, the ballet, who done-its, and old and new friendships.

neighborhood_overview:
The Inner Mission District- "La Mision" is a great place to land in SF because of it's central location & close access to downtown.
It is the city's Latino district & has been the gateway for most new immigrants, initially Italian, Irish, then predominantly Latino since the 1960's , more recent arrivals are the artists, hipsters & even more recent, the techies.
The community is famous for its historic buildings, Mission burritos (the best in the US), grungy artistic scene, it's colorful murals & political organizing.
The neighborhood has a continued history of immigrant rights & before that the Chicano civil rights movement of the 1960's. In spite of all the recent gentrification the community is still 48% Latino.

host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.
- See the Zapatista Mural in Jack Kerouc Alley, painted by a dear friend &  behind iconic City Lights Bookstore .  Ask me about the mural story.
-Catch a baseball game at Oracle park !

* Telegraph Hill the most beautiful of San Francisco’s Hills. Intimate and delightful. Possibly also the USA's most famous hill
* One block to the lively cafes, restaurants, bars of North Beach, yet quiet
* Oldest part of San Francisco, part of pre-Gold Rush Yerba Buena
* Rebuilt after 1906 earthquake
* Telegraph Hill got name from pole-and-arm signal station, precursor of internet
* Nearby Coit Tower has perhaps the greatest of urban vistas anywhere

* Adjacent to Barbary Coast, former red light district of late 1800s, containing remaining buildings to escape 1906 earthquake and fire
* Beatnik movement centered here, in Caffe Trieste, Vesuv

neighborhood_overview:
About the Inner Mission District-
"La Mision"
Centrally located close to downtown, it is the city's Latino district & has been the gateway for most new immigrants, initially Italian, Irish, then predominantly Latino since the 1970's .
It is famous for its historic buildings, Mission burritos (the best in Northern California), grungy artistic scene & it's colorful murals.
Though the Mission still retains it's gritty 'barrio' (hood) flavor the neighborhood has been undergoing a second wave of gentrification lately and has been experiencing with an influx of technology money.
The Mission district is large & complex, with varying socioeconomic areas, clusters of mini-communities, and specialty stores found nowhere else. A few years back Utne Reader rated the Inner Mission the 2nd coolest place to live in the US (first was New Orlean's Garden District).
Like in any other cities there are sections of the Mission that can be high crime but don't let that scare y
host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.
- See the Zapatista Mural in Jack Kerouc Alley, painted by a dear friend &  behind iconic City Lights Bookstore .  Ask me about the mural story.
-Catch a baseball game at Oracle park !
SF songs & bands : 
City Lights by Journey
The Grateful Dead of course
Huey Lewis & the News 
Carlos Santana  & more !

description:

High-end finishes and amenities throughout, wonderful indoor-outdoor living spaces, and virtually everything you could possibly need within 2-5 blocks. Andy is a life-long traveler, thrilled to finally be back home in the Bay Area where he grew up and where his extended family still resides.  In 2008 Andy and his wife Tanya were fortunate to find a classic Noe Valley fixer-upper and moved into the cute, tiny Pioneer Victorian where they lived for almost 6 years.  In 2013 they began a complete reconstruction of the 1880's cottage and in 2014 moved their family back into a completely transformed contemporary house equipped for this millenium's lifestyle - the Victorian front remains, but everything behind it now meets the needs and expectations of today (hello, closets and gigabit ethernet...).  Andy has been an at-home Dad since 2000, and has worked in tourism, academia, and as a professional chef.  He loves the vibrant food culture in San Francisco and only wishes he had more time to take advantage of all the amazing arts that San Francisco dishes up on a daily basis as well as the wonderful outdoor spaces, hikes, and bike rides that are nearby.  Andy is very knowledgeable about San Francisco food and fun and is happy to make suggestions to help your stay be enjoyable, fun and tasty, whether you are here for business or family pleasure.

Andy has enjoyed a wide variety of travel styles and accommodations over the years, from $3/night huts on beaches in Eastern Indonesia, simple Ryokan in Japan, and luxury hotels and chateaux in the US, Asia and Europe: the apartment is equipped to closely match the experience of a boutique hotel - luxury finishes throughout and thoughtful amenities - but with a lot more space than most boutique hotels provide!

neighborhood_overview:
SAN FRANCISCO – Dogpatch is proof that good things come in small packages. The charming microhood was largely industrial for years, but has become a budding enclave of artisans and craftsmen. The area maintains a sleepy, untouched vibe on the surface — with palpitating creativity at the core.

The historic district is home to some of the city’s oldest structures and Victorian cottages. Pier 70 is an existing shipyard and industrial site that supported both World Wars and manufactured supplies for the Gold Rush and Transcontinental Railway. The Noonan Building at Pier 70 is now studio space.

There are so many hidden gems in Russian Hill.

For starters, it is one of San Francisco's 49 hills, and one of its original "Seven Hills". The neighborhood's name goes back to the Gold Rush era, when settlers discovered a small Russian cemetery at the top of the hill. Russian naval and merchant ships frequently visited San Francisco throughout the 19th century beginning in 1806, and there are several mentions of burials of crew members in the Russian Hill cemetery in the first half of the century. The cemetery was removed, but the name remains to this day.

Named for Mission Dolores founded in 1776, San Francisco’s oldest neighborhood has some of its hottest new restaurants and galleries. Bernal Heights, Potrero Hill These neighborhoods all share a sunny outlook. Boasting some of the best weather in the city, the Mission District, Bernal Heights and Potrero Hill take advantage of an abundance of fog-free days. New restaurants and night spots are a draw while Mission Dolores, 16th and Dolores streets, is the oldest structure in San Francisco. Many of the city’s pioneers are buried in an adjacent cemetery. Potrero Hill’s Dogpatch neighborhood is one of 11 historic districts in the city and home to the second crookedest street (after Lombard) in the city.

The neighborhood's name goes back to the Gold Rush era, when settlers discovered a small Russian cemetery at the top of the hill. Russian naval and merchant ships frequently visited San Francisco throughout the 19th century beginning in 1806, back when it was called Yerba Buena and was part of the Spanish/Mexican empire. The cemetery has since been removed, but the name remains to this day.

With so much history in the area, you'll discover something fun and unique around every corner.

Noe Valley is a very unique, sunny and family friendly neighborhood with great weather. Noe survived the 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire thanks to the “golden fire plug” that keep working where the water system elsewhere failed. Historic Victorians, Edwardians, sprinkled with new modern homes and mash-ups of both are characteristic in the neighborhood – an architecture lovers walking neighborhood. Many local restaurants, cafes, boutiques, and Walgreens and Whole Foods are 3 blocks away along 24th Street. Close to the Mission District’s exciting restaurants, cafes, and urban culture. Noe Valley retains a mixed age demographic and is very popular with techies who work in media, software, and internet due to quick access in and out of the city to head south to Silicon Valley.

neighborhood_overview:
Nob Hill is one of San Francisco’s historic "Seven Hills" and has long been a symbol of luxury and prestige. The neighborhood rose to prominence in the late 19th century when wealthy railroad tycoons built their grand mansions there, drawn by the area’s commanding views and the convenience of the newly invented cable car, which made the steep incline accessible.

Today, Nob Hill retains its historic charm while blending with modern urban vibrancy. It is known for its elegant architecture, including landmarks like the iconic Fairmont Hotel, Grace Cathedral, and the Mark Hopkins Hotel, which showcase the grandeur of the area’s past. While many of the original mansions were lost in the 1906 earthquake and fire, the neighborhood has evolved into a lively hub with upscale hotels, fine dining, and a large population of young urban professionals.

Its central location makes it a perfect spot for exploring nearby attractions. Nob Hill is surrounded by the Financial District

Russian Hill has evolved into a chic residential neighborhood with outstanding views from every corner. Combined with several great cafes, restaurants, antique shops and boutiques, it’s easy to see why any visitor would gladly leave their heart in San Francisco. Cars line up day after day to drive down nearby Lombard Street, the “crookedest” street in the world, and make the slow creep downhill past charming period homes. Polk Street is the main drag in this neighborhood, where you will find trendy bars, cafes and shops populated with locals, but for one of the most charming rides in the city, grab a cable car heading up and down Hyde Street. Aquatic Park and it's small beach are 3 blocks north. The western edge of Fisherman's Wharf and the Buena Vista Cafe, with it's famous Irish Coffees, is two blocks further (east). It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

neighborhood_overview:
• SoMa's multifaceted character brings together all sorts of people. Tech-savvy entrepreneurs rub elbows with well-read bohemian types, and museum curators share the sidewalks with ill-groomed individuals.

• Most of the action can be found at MOSCONE CENTER, SF MOMA, and Yerba Buena Gardens, Giants ballpark. SoMa, as it's known, sounds a little like a SoHo wannabe, and it does have a strong downtown vibe. Restaurants, Hip bars, clubs, and specialty coffee cafes are all around.

Drink tea with good company or just by myself with a book in hand. And! when I'm feeling like being silly... I love to wear sparkly and furry outfits and go dancing with friends.

description: Our social and vibrant hostel in downtown SF is the place to stay! We invite travelers and adventurers of all ages, from all corners of the globe, to rest their heads at this historic hostel in the heart of San Francisco. neighborhood_overview: Our hostel is located in the culturally rich neighborhood of North Beach (SF’s Little Italy) and borders America’s largest Chinatown. host_about:
There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. At first glance, one might presume that the endgame of all hostels is to create a sense of firm familiarity among guest and staff alike, but with us, you can feel it. With a full roster of events that are ongoing, all inclusive in both experience and price, and a design purposefully conducive to the gathering of folks all around the world, we are dedicated to establishing a world reaching community that you feel while you are here, and long after your stay.

Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

host_about:
I live in a beautifully, newly decorated home by the Pacific Ocean.  I love the ocean.  The  fresh, crisp air that it brings rejuvenates me.  The ocean also reminds me of the far off lands I have visited, and the friends I have made when doing so.  Europe (Germany, Spain, Italy, Turkey), Mexico, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, and of course, where I am from, China, are just some of the places I have traveled.

China holds my fondest memories, not  because I was born there, but because China is where I learned all about cosmetology and the holistic healing arts.  I was a successful, award winning Cosmetologist in China, and moved to the United States to seek even greater opportunities. Today, I own several successful businesses, and help thousands of people achieve the beauty they desire.  However, what I really enjoy, is in sharing the richness of our cultural diversity with others...that is what makes America great. Our country has the ability to weave many diverse cultures  into a beautiful fabric that unifies all of us.  I truly look forward to sharing with others, and making their stay the most memorable experience possible.

description:
Are you a bootstrapping founder or a techie lacking a private room budget in this crazy-expensive city? Then share a room with your peers or with some other people with the same mindset. Enjoy the community and a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment without breaking your piggy bank. The ideal landing pad for entrepreneurs and other builders/hustlers in San Francisco!

For more information about our houses feel free to check:

HACKNSLEEP,COM
neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood is called Nob Hill. You’ll be right around the corner from shops, coffee houses, restaurants, bars on Polk street, and grocery stores including Trader Joe’s and Whole Foods. Take a jog down to China town, or a walk over to Fisherman’s Wharf. A 15 minute bike ride puts you right in the Financial District for an easy commute to and from work. We love the Contraband coffee bar just 2 blocks over for a great atmosphere to work and sip your favorite pour over brew. Everything you need is easy to get to!
host_about:
Welcome to HacknSleep! Hacknsleep provides a landing pad for entrepreneurs, designers, coders, engineers and other innovators and builders from the broader startup community.

When staying with us, you'll meet like-minded individuals with a culture of pragmatic cooperation and collaboration. We are more than just about housing. We care, build trusted relationships, and support each other in achieving our goals and startup visions. 

We offer private and shared bedrooms that allow even bootstrapping founders to live in a great neighborhood and the friendly, clean, convenient, and safe place they deserve. 

We partner with startup accelerators, bootcamps, coding academies, and co-working spaces and prefer recruiting our residents through peer-recommendations and our networks. So please let us know how you have heard from us.

I am also an entrepreneur and builder who now runs an international startup accelerator out of Palo Alto, SF, and NYC. When I bring founders from abroad, one of the hardest challenges for them is to find appropriate housing. That's why I stepped up and created Bed|n|Build.

We love social, easy going, and low maintenance folks. After all, it's a co-living place with diverse people from the different corners of this world. Nerdy - sure. Geeky - also welcome. 

Don't reach out if others have described you as picky, high maintenance, or a drama king or queen. Also, do not contact us if you are not interested in getting to know the other builders sharing the house or joining the Happy Hours that we organize for the community occasionally.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Historical Telegraph Hill ( VERY SAFE AREA)
Now: The iconic Coit Tower is the focal point of the area for most visitors, but if you're willing to take your time and wander (and hike a couple of steep stretches of steps) you can catch a lot of extra scenery. Many people take the Greenwich Street steps since they are closest to the tower, and return the same way. The Filbert Street steps, just to the south, lead through much more of the lush landscaping characteristic of Telegraph Hill. Our neighborhood is also known for supporting a flock of feral parrots, primarily red-masked parakeets (Aratinga erythrogenys), descended from escaped or released pets. The flock was popularized by a book and subsequent documentary (2003), both titled The Wild Parrots of Telegraph Hill.

Then: The name Telegraph Hill came from a structure built on the top of the hill in the mid-1800s, which would visually signal the city with regard to the type of vessels passing through the Golden Gate.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

name: Luxury Garden Suite by the Ocean
description: A spacious, thoughtfully detailed suite with a private entrance, a private garden, and a private one-car garage. Walk out the door, and you are steps from San Francisco’s most beautiful landmarks: Lands End, Ocean Beach, the Sutro Baths, and the Golden Gate.
neighborhood_overview:
The suite is at the northwest tip of San Francisco, a quiet part of the city, surrounded by nature. Stroll to Ocean Beach and catch the sunset over the Pacific Ocean. Cross the street to the Lands End trail, where you can see red-tailed hawks and dolphins (and unbeatable views of the Golden Gate Bridge). Walk down the hill to explore Golden Gate Park’s bison paddock, waterfalls, and Japanese tea garden.

The neighborhood offers an array of cultural experiences. Check out the world-class art exhibits at the Legion of Honor and the deYoung museum. Attend a music festival or free concert in Golden Gate Park.

Foodies will love it here. If you want international cuisine, check out the local Chinese, Thai, Japanese, Vietnamese, and Burmese restaurants, many of which are among the best in the city. Or get a coffee at the local cafe, Simple Pleasures, the oldest coffee roaster in San Francisco and a good spot for live music and $5 craft beers on tap.

neighborhood_overview: The original site of the Ghirardelli Chocolate Factory (previously a woolen mill), are now the home of a stylish collection of shops and restaurants—one of the most pleasant places to stroll and shop in the city. Wind through passageways and across plazas to visit an assortment of boutiques and gift shops, or relax with bay views from a selection of restaurants. If you have kids along, you probably have one destination in mind more than any other: the Ghirardelli Soda Fountain and Chocolate Shop. The line can be out the door but don’t worry—it moves fast. Soon you’ll be facing the staggering menu of sundae choices: Will it be the family-size “Earthquake”? (Eight scoops, eight toppings, bananas, whipped cream, almonds, chocolate chips, and cherries.) Or maybe have a “Gold Rush” (vanilla ice cream with hot fudge and peanut butter throughout).

neighborhood_overview:
Music City Hotel is located in the vibrant Polk Gulch/Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe.

Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

description:

neighborhood_overview:
--Parkside Square & Bob Cheney Field (3 blocks)
My kid's favorite playground!

--Pine Lake Park (2 blocks)
This natural area with a valley & lake also offers trails & a wide range of migratory birds.

--Stern Grove Park: (~ 0.2miles)
It consists of several park sections including the Concert Meadow, the West Meadow, and Pine Lake Park. The grove's Pine Lake is one of three natural lakes in the city of San Francisco. Since 1938, there have been weekly concerts and performances in the outdoor amphitheater during the summer months. Supported entirely by contributions, the concerts have always been free to the public. Crowds have often exceeded 20,000 persons.
--San Francisco Zoo & Gardens (~1 miles)
Most of popular! The zoo housed more than one thousand individual animals, representing more than 250 species.

--Cafe & Restaurants (~0.3 miles)

Riverside Seafood Restaurant (Chinese)
Dumpling Kitchen (Chinese)
Ming's

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

neighborhood_overview:
Noe Valley is a quiet neighborhood, like a village within a city! It is kind of unique in having about the densest concentration of original Victorian homes dating from the 1850s until about the 1906 earthquake. The reason for the prevalence of old Victorians (like mine!) is that Noe Valley was miraculously saved from the fire after the 1906 Earthquake because the fire hydrant at 20th and Church Streets was the very first found with actual water pressure as the fire raced southwest from the downtown. It helped create a firebreak at 20th St. Today you can see 20th century buildings on the North side of 20th and 19th century Victorians on the south side all the way through Noe Valley. Now that famous hydrant is regularly and lovingly painted gold.

name: (#3) 3BR 1Ba Renovated Flat in the heart of SoMA
description:
Extraordinary location close to everything. 1.5 blocks to BART/Muni. This is Unit #3 in a 5-unit 1920's Edwardian building on a quiet street in SoMa, fully remodeled in 2018. It has an open kitchen/living area with eating bar. Each bedroom has a large closet & a work desk. Lease can be 1 month to 1 year.

Perfect for a group that is new to the area and needs a place to land with no hassle, or doesn't have their own furniture. An easy way get to know the City. Good wifi for working from home.
neighborhood_overview: One hundred year ago, SoMa (or South-of-Market) was built with wide boulevards that held warehouses or factories on the corners and perimeter of each block. Nowadays, these are converted apartments or loft buildings.  The interior of the large blocks contained smaller street and were quiet "Residential Enclaves" of two- and three- story Edwardian flats, built with the last of the redwood from nearby forests in the 1910s and 20s. These enclaves today are hidden clusters of refurbished older homes that feel neighborly and almost private.  It's a highly walkable neighborhood with many bars, restaurants and clubs along the main roads, yet quiet and residential inside. Mid-SoMa, where we are, is very close to City Hall, a 1.5 block walk to Civic Center BART and Muni (which can get you anywhere in the region), easily walkable to Moscone Convention Center and the Financial and Hotel districts. Shopping at Union Square is about four blocks away!
host_about: I have lived in San Francisco for 30 years with a brief stint in Denver . My parents are in Asheville and it has become my second home over the last few years. I'm now here more than half-time. I am the co-founder the AIDS Memorial Quilt, which started on my back porch in 1987 (Younger people have no clue what this is, but a online search should help...) I've been running AIDS or LGBT organizations my whole adult life and enjoy the community-building aspect of what I do.  I recently retired as executive director of AIDS Emergency Fund and Breast Cancer Emergency Fund, two related non-profits that help low income people pay their basic living costs while disabled or going through surgery, chemo or radiation.  I am grateful to the many hosts on Airbnb who have opened their homes to me when I travel, and I was inspired by them top remodel this farmhouse for your enjoyment.

neighborhood_overview: San Francisco Marina District -The Marina District in named for its proximity to San Francisco's yacht harbors and the bay front walkway, but is known for its million dollar Mediterranean homes and its numerous restaurants and boutiques.The nearby Marina Green and Crissy Field are popular for jogging, windsurfing, and enjoying the spectacular views of the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz and yachts sailing the Bay. host_about:
Built by the son of a California Gold Rush miner, the historic Marina Motel was built to celebrate the opening of the Golden Gate Bridge in the late 1930's and is still run by the same family. Ideally situated between Fisherman's Wharf and the Golden Gate Bridge in the popular Marina District, the Marina Motel offers a one-of-a-kind, old world experience. The first impression one has upon stepping into the motel's cobblestone courtyard is "Wow! This is like a little oasis back here with birds chirping, flowers EVERYWHERE, cute little garages and rooms decorated to feel like home. I feel like I'm in Europe."

Walk around the corner to the numerous outdoor cafes, restaurants and boutiques on Chestnut and Union Street, take a walk on the beach to the Golden Gate Bridge or rent a bike and ride across it while taking the ferry back, ride a cable car at Fisherman's Wharf or visit the de Young Museum or California Academy of Science in Golden Gate Park. The best of San Francisco is within easy reach.

neighborhood_overview:
Noe Valley is a quiet neighborhood, like a village within a city! It is kind of unique in having about the densest concentration of original Victorian homes dating from the 1850s until about the 1906 earthquake. The reason for the prevalence of old Victorians (like mine!) is that Noe Valley was miraculously saved from the fire after the 1906 Earthquake because the fire hydrant at 20th and Church Streets was the very first found with actual water pressure as the fire raced southwest from the downtown. It helped create a firebreak at 20th St. Today you can see 20th century buildings on the North side of 20th and 19th century Victorians on the south side all the way through Noe Valley. Now that famous hydrant is regularly and lovingly painted gold.

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to the vibrant Castro neighborhood in San Francisco, one of the most historic and diverse areas in the city. Known for its rich cultural heritage, this neighborhood is a popular destination for locals and tourists alike. The Castro has played a significant role in the LGBTQ+ community since the 1970s, and it continues to be a symbol of acceptance, inclusivity, and equality.

With its colorful streets, charming shops, and lively nightlife, the Castro offers a unique experience for visitors. Here, you can explore the historic Castro Theatre, which has been entertaining audiences since 1922. You can also discover the Castro's many art galleries, vintage boutiques, and antique shops. Take a stroll along the Rainbow Honor Walk, which celebrates the achievements of LGBTQ+ pioneers, or visit the Harvey Milk Plaza, named after the civil rights leader who lived in the neighborhood.

The Castro is also home to some of San Francisco's best restaurants, cafes, and bars.

name: Urban oasis!  Deck, city views, entire place
description:
Welcome to San Francisco! Looking for the perfect place to stay while visiting the city? Look no further than this charming and contemporary studio that offers panoramic views of the city's skyline and a glimpse of the iconic GG Bridge from your private deck.
Located just a short walk from Mission, you'll be able to explore the city easily. Whether you're in town for business or pleasure, this urban paradise will make you feel right at home. A bonus - easy street parking! Book your stay today!
neighborhood_overview:
Peralta Heights is a hidden urban oasis on the sunny north slope of Bernal Heights - one of SF's lesser-known best neighborhoods! This neighborhood offers residents an urban-suburban mix feel; there are a lot of bars, restaurants, coffee shops, and parks, but also lots of urban trail hikes and serene gardens with stunning views over the city.
Many of the Peralta Heights residences are relatively historic, built no later than 1939 and quite a bit earlier in some cases. You'll find a mix of old-timers living here for a few decades, with more recently moving young professionals appreciating the diversity of this location.
Peralta Heights has excellent public transportation and is very bikeable.

Nearby neighborhoods: Bernal Heights, Mission District, Potrero Hill, Holly Park, and Dolores Heights.

Dynamic spirit, live for traveling and travel for living...and for work.

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

name: Modern family home in the sunny Mission
description: With high ceilings, ample skylights, a sunny garden and lots of character, our spacious family home is warm and inviting. It's conveniently located in the very walkable and colorful neighborhood of the Inner Mission. From dive bars to Michelin starred restaurants, it's a foodie heaven that still maintains a strong neighborhood vibe. Our historic house was redesigned to include open living areas, and has a large garage with fast access to the highway to get to the East Bay or the Peninsula.
neighborhood_overview:
As our neighbor says, the Mission is like the Brooklyn of SF, it’s both beautiful and grungy. It has a bit of everything: colorful murals celebrating its Latino heritage, new Michelin starred restaurants, classic taquerias and panaderías, dive bars and swanky cocktail spots, taco trucks and so many neighborhood spots to join locals for an overpriced but amazing pour-over coffee.

Our home is situated in a special area called the Inner Mission that is relatively quiet and neighborhood-y but has so much to offer that it's buzzing on the weekends with locals from all over San Francisco. Our neighborhood is a sunny spot in a city otherwise known for fog. Dolores Park, Billy Goat Hill and Bernal Heights Parks - all minutes away - are just some of the places to hike and catch a breathtaking view of our beautiful city.

host_about:
Greetings!

My name is Warren C. Lathe III, I go by Trey (a nickname, means "3" :). I am a career biologist (molecular genetics) though currently, I'm writing, teaching and other things (like Airbnb!). 

My partner in crime since 1996, and legal husband since 2008, is Guy and we have two school-age (middle and high schools) children (the picture here was 8 years ago :D). Guy is an English as a Second Language teacher by training and career, but now manages properties.

We have a long and deep connection to San Francisco. Guy is a Berryessa. The Berryessa's settled San Francisco and the bay in the 1770s coming with the De Anza party in 1776. His GGrandfather was Jose de los Santos Berryessa.  Guy's parents were married and lived in this city during the '40s (while his father fought in the Pacific theater). My own parents moved to the Bay Area in the 80's. Guy and I both moved into this home in 1997. San Francisco had been our dream city for its acceptance, tolerance, family heritage and its beauty. It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

name: Glen Park pied-à-terre
description:
Welcome to my cozy home in Glen Park, where I’ve lived for over 30 years. This is a Goldilocks-sized two-bedroom, 1.5-bath home located in one of the most charming neighborhoods in San Francisco.

Glen Park has a grocery store, coffee shop, adorable restaurants nearby, a vast park, and easy access to public transportation, including BART access to downtown, both airports and the greater Bay Area. You are near the on-ramps to 280 and 101 for easy driving access.
neighborhood_overview:
I’ve found Glen Park to be the perfect place to enjoy a peaceful pace of life, while still feeling connected to the vibrant city of San Francisco. The neighborhood has a quaint, almost village-like feel that’s rare to find in while still being inside the city of San Francisco. With its quiet streets and welcoming community, it's easy to take morning walks through the neighborhood to Glen Canyon Park. The local library, just a short stroll away offers a cozy place to sit with a good book and enjoy the company of other residents.

The commercial hub around Bosworth and Diamond Streets has everything you would need. For Breakfast, you can start your day with a visit to Glen Park Café, formerly known as Tyger’s, where the friendly staff know the regular's orders: order a stack of fluffy pancakes and a hot cup of coffee. From there, it’s off to the Canyon Market for some fresh produce, and then perhaps a stop at Bird & Beckett, the local bookstore that feels more like a community
host_about: I’m Karen, a retired schoolteacher. I love spending time with my grandchildren, family, and friends. I’m a fan of history and books, especially fiction. I’m an avid traveler, and I’m passionate about exploring the many art museums here in San Francisco. I look forward to welcoming you into my home!

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.
